title: clamp_current 'last_question_id' fallback branch is masked by its dedicated test
detail: q_param=Some("free_text") is a valid answered id, so the case hits branch 'True, Some(id), _ -> id' (form_handler.gleam:266), never the '_, _, None -> last_question_id(slot)' fallback (line 269). The test cannot fail if last_question_id regresses; it claims to pin the fallback but doesn't.
recommended_fix: Add a case with an invalid/None q_param when all keys are answered, e.g. clamp_current(LandlordRef, Some("bogus"), all_keys, None), asserting it equals the last question id.

title: resend_audit_details no-PII assertions are vacuous (fixture detail carries no PII)
evidence:
messages.ChannelOutcome(messages.Email, messages.Delivered, "email-id"),
      messages.ChannelOutcome(
        messages.Sms,
        messages.Skipped,
        "twilio not configured",
      ),
    ])
  let text = json.to_string(details)
  string.contains(text, "delivered") |> should.be_true
  string.contains(text, "email") |> should.be_true
  string.contains(text, "@") |> should.be_false
  string.contains(text, "+353") |> should.be_false
detail: The ChannelOutcome detail fields ("email-id", "twilio not configured") contain neither '@' nor '+353', so the should.be_false assertions pass even if a future regression appends o.detail to the audit JSON. The audit_log row shape is a load-bearing contract; the no-PII guard is untestable as written.
recommended_fix: Use a PII-bearing fixture detail (e.g. "recipient@example.com" / "+353861234567") so the absence assertions become load-bearing against a detail-leak regression.
